newsitem.title: UK: London's favourite red bus heads for end of road.
newsitem.headline: London's favourite red bus heads for end of road.

text.p: London's favourite red bus, the open-platformed Routemaster, is to be phased out by 2001.
London Transport said on Monday the ageing buses, as much a symbol of the capital as the Houses of Parliament and Buckingham Palace, would cost too much to refurbish.
London has 600 Routemasters, some of them 40 years old and with more than one million miles (1.6 million km) on the clock.
Phasing out the Routemasters is likely to provoke the same public uproar as when British Telecom tried to get rid of the familiar red telephone box.
When newer buses with automatic passenger doors were added to the London Transport fleet a few years ago, traditionalists derided them as "biscuit tins", devoid of any kind of style.
"The Routemasters are very much liked both by the public and by tourists," said a London Transport spokesman.

Routemasters, complete with conductors urging passengers to "Hold very tight, please", mostly ply central London routes, providing a familiar backdrop to Oxford Street, Regent Street and Trafalgar Square.
London Transport said it had asked bus manufacturers about building a replacement Routemaster, but the costs were too high, given the relatively small numbers needed.

Passengers hopping on and off the open rear platform of the Routemasters are four times more likely to have an accident than when they travel on the buses with automatic doors, which will take over as replacements.
